analysis:
Independently examined the supplied analysis, replayed patches, metadata and source excerpts. The added .github/workflows/ci-dev-hourly.yml:9–38 automatically dispatches ci-dev.yml on dev. Its dispatcher uses a GitHub-hosted runner, a three-minute timeout, explicit actions:write/contents:read permissions, no checkout, quoted repository context and a fixed workflow/ref. API failures stop execution. No concrete token disclosure, shell injection or change to provider encryption, cache isolation (T-041), authorization (T-052/T-053), privileged operations or billing is established.
The changelog and docs/developer/build.md additions describe the same dispatch path; the updated date and supplied unchanged native dependency-closure documentation introduce no security control changes. The unfinished-run query at workflow HEAD:31–37 is bounded to 20 results and is not atomic, so it does not guarantee the documentation's no-overlap claim. A security impact is not established without downstream runner/resource behavior.
Material integration uncertainty remains: ci-dev.yml as defined on dev is not supplied. Review its workflow_dispatch admission, permissions, secret access, runner selection and artifact/cache handling to establish whether this new automatic execution path preserves build qualification boundaries (A-017/T-054) and avoids exposing privileged CI resources to less-trusted branch code. Missing implementation is not proof of a regression. Replay is incomplete (two source units omitted), so earlier claims about additional documentation context could not be independently verified. No supported finding qualifies within the supplied scope.
